audits.title: Clinical audit to assess diagnosis and severity stratification of acute pancreatitis
audits.standard: National guidelines and the Atlanta criteria for diagnosis and severity stratification of acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: University Hospital Lewisham, general surgery department

cycle1.result: Severity scoring completed in 33% and used incorrectly in the majority; almost half of CT scans were deemed unnecessary.

audits.intervention: Acute pancreatitis protocol created with Upper GI surgeons (re-audit not yet reported).
audits.other_findings: Significant shortfalls in interventions for alcohol and gallstone cases.
audits.citation: Woods H, Roberts R, Bradley R. Clinical audit to assess diagnosis and severity stratification of acute pancreatitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad388.037.

audits.title: ThP5.3 - A Clinical Audit on Assessing Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Improving the use of the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria and outcomes
audits.standard: Glasgow-Imrie Criteria scoring on admission for acute pancreatitis; scores ≥3 reviewed by senior and/or HDU/ITU

cycle1.result: 44% (22/50) of patients were scored using the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria.

audits.intervention: Presentation, posters and email, then a scoring tick box in the electronic clerking notes

cycle2.result: 84% (49/58) scored; escalation of scores ≥3 rose from 17% to 100%.

audits.other_findings: After the first intervention 66% (21/32) were scored; mean length of stay fell from 14.5 to 11 days and documentation completeness rose from 78% to 96%.
audits.citation: Nazar N, Read P, Bolton H, Bailey C. ThP5.3 - A Clinical Audit on Assessing Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Improving the use of the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria and outcomes. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.277.

audits.title: 379 Improving Documentation of Severity Scores in Acute Pancreatitis: A Two-Cycle Audit Against AUGIS Guidelines
audits.standard: AUGIS/BSG: all acute pancreatitis patients to have a validated severity score documented within 48 hours of admission
audits.intervention: FY/SHO teaching, staff posters summarising guidelines and an electronic documentation template.

cycle2.result: 7 (30%) had severity scores documented, all within the first 24 hours; one further case incomplete due to pending labs.

audits.other_findings: Scores used were Glasgow-Imrie, Modified Glasgow and BISAP according to clinician preference.
audits.citation: Alwani O, Abdelwahab A, Onah N, Arshad Z, McWilliams A. 379 Improving Documentation of Severity Scores in Acute Pancreatitis: A Two-Cycle Audit Against AUGIS Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_17). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf270.132.

audits.title: 28 Improving Monitoring and Severity Stratification in Acute Pancreatitis: A Quality Improvement Study Using BISAP Score Implementation
audits.standard: NICE and BSG guidelines on severity stratification, observations and escalation in acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Severity scores documented in 10%; monitoring inconsistent.

audits.intervention: BISAP score introduced through educational sessions and a printed format added to clerking proformas.
audits.other_findings: Fluid balance, observations and investigation documentation also improved.
audits.citation: Kaur J, Agrawal K, Dawood E, Jagra G. 28 Improving Monitoring and Severity Stratification in Acute Pancreatitis: A Quality Improvement Study Using BISAP Score Implementation. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_17). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf270.304.

audits.title: 117 Initial Severity Assessment in Patients with Acute Pancreatitis in a UK District General Hospital: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: International Association of Pancreatology guidance on initial severity assessment (Modified Atlanta Classification)
audits.setting: Large UK district general hospital, West Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: None had a formal severity assessment recorded.

audits.intervention: Pancreatitis Severity Scoring proforma with Modified Atlanta criteria in e-care, plus education at M&M meetings, junior doctor inductions and multidisciplinary awareness campaigns.

cycle2.result: 66.6% (18/27) had a proforma completed, of which 38.8% (7/18) were fully completed.

audits.other_findings: Only a minority of proformas were fully completed; further education and re-audit are planned.
audits.citation: Patel K, Symes M, Patel K. 117 Initial Severity Assessment in Patients with Acute Pancreatitis in a UK District General Hospital: A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.409.

audits.title: TPW 7.16 Improving Compliance with Severity Scoring in Acute Pancreatitis: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: severity scoring within 48 hours of admission
audits.setting: District general hospital, Altnagelvin Area Hospital; acute pancreatitis admissions

cycle1.result: 2 of 12 (16.7%) had a Glasgow Imrie score recorded.

audits.intervention: Targeted teaching for resident doctors and a process for the on-call team to ensure scoring of all new admissions.
audits.other_findings: In cycle 1 one patient with score ≥3 was not escalated until day five and needed ICU for ARDS; no ICU admissions in cycle 2.
audits.citation: Majdoubeh Y, Marzouk A, Elnagar M. TPW 7.16 Improving Compliance with Severity Scoring in Acute Pancreatitis: A Two-Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.385.

audits.title: Acute Pancreatitis Management and Scoring in the Department of General Surgery, Northwick Park Hospital, 2022-2024.
audits.standard: NICE NG104; modified Atlanta, Modified Marshall and Glasgow-Imrie scoring on admission and at 48 hours
audits.setting: Department of General Surgery, Northwick Park Hospital

cycle1.result: 30% had documented scoring on admission; none had repeat scoring at 48 hours; Atlanta scoring on admission and at 48 hours 0%.

audits.intervention: Departmental teaching, posters, and email and messaging reminders.

cycle2.result: Admission scoring 40%; Atlanta scoring on admission and at 48 hours 7.5%.

audits.citation: Awan B, Elsaigh M, Watfah J. Acute Pancreatitis Management and Scoring in the Department of General Surgery, Northwick Park Hospital, 2022-2024. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e100172. doi:10.7759/cureus.100172. PMID: 41458339.
